the American political system is a two party system and it's almost always been an A or B choice

Nobody ever declared that the system shall be 2-party, nor hailed that lack of choice as being good for the people. It's the other way round - people implemented First Past The Post (or 'most votes wins') because it's simple, without realising that mathematically it ensures a 2-party system will emerge.

The reason is something called the spoiler effect, which is definitely worth looking up, though the basic problem is that an 80% conservative country can lose power to the 20% liberal parasites if the commies form one party while the normal people form 8 different varieties of conservatism with 10% support each. While AV may not be problem-free, such as still not being proportional and still probably weak to gerrymandering, it does at least kill the spoiler effect and thus the 2-party system.

I like to think of it as a direct upgrade to FPTP since it is actually compatible - an FPTP ballot is actually just an AV ballot with only one candidate ranked, which is still correct to do in AV if all others are equally indifferent to you. If you have ever voted 'tactically' in FPTP because your main pick would be a 'wasted' vote so you voted for whoever is likely to keep out your most hated candidate instead, you need AV since it has that mechanism built in.
